articles.headline: Inside the Jordan Dome, where 'Space Jam' pickup games helped MJ get his game back
articles.description: Thirty years after "Space Jam," those who shared the summer with Jordan remember the basketball that unfolded offscreen.

images.name: Space Jam 4 [608x342]
images.caption: Thirty years after "Space Jam," those who shared the summer with Jordan remember the basketball that unfolded offscreen.

images.name: Space Jam 2 [608x342]
images.caption: Between scenes with Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, Jordan was preparing for a season that would end with 72 wins and another championship.

images.name: Space Jam 3 [608x342]
images.caption: Jordan's supporting cast extended beyond the Looney Tunes, with NBA stars filling a custom-built gym on the Warner Bros. lot.

images.name: Space Jam 1 [608x342]
images.caption: The competition inside the Jordan Dome needed no Hollywood embellishment: Players remember pickup games with playoff-level intensity.

images.name: Space Jam 5 [608x342]
images.caption: "Space Jam" brought Jordan to Hollywood, but his basketball ambitions shaped what happened away from the cameras.

images.name: Miller MJ
images.caption: Jordan held a 36-20 edge over Miller in their 56 NBA meetings, including a 4-3 record in playoff games.
images.credit: Nathaniel S. Butler/NBAE via Getty Images

images.name: Michael Jordan Dennis Rodman
images.caption: While Rodman never appeared on screen in "Space Jam," his participation in pickup games at the Jordan Dome helped pave the way for his arrival in Chicago.
